lesson.summary: A global ecommerce company based in Seattle expands to Ireland and Asia to be closer to its customers. It deploys in several Regions for speed, uses multiple Availability Zones for resilience, and encrypts its own data. Security is shared: AWS secures the physical data centers, and the company secures its data and cloud resources.
keyPoints: Deploying in Regions near customers reduces latency
Multiple Availability Zones keep an application running when one zone fails
Using more than one Region adds resilience for the whole application
AWS secures the physical infrastructure, so the company does not secure the data center itself
The company secures and encrypts its own data and cloud resources
lesson.simpleSummary: A company in one country grows worldwide. It opens AWS Regions near its customers so pages load faster, spreads its systems across zones so one failure does not stop the shop, and keeps control of its own data.
lesson.mnemonic: Naruto hint: Like Naruto training in several villages at once, the company places its ninja closer to every customer.

scenarios.text: A company based in Seattle wants to serve customers in Ireland and Australia with fast page loads, and it wants the store to stay online if one location fails.

questions.prompt: A company in Seattle wants its customers in Ireland to get faster page loads. What is the best first step?

options.text: Buy servers and ship them to Ireland
Deploy the application in an AWS Region in Europe, such as eu-west-1 in Ireland
Serve all customers from a single data center in Seattle
Store the data on a laptop in the Seattle office

questions.explanation: Placing resources in a Region near the customers reduces latency. eu-west-1 is the Ireland Region, which has three Availability Zones. Shipping servers and serving from Seattle add distance, and a laptop is not a reliable data store.
questions.simplePrompt: A company in Seattle wants its customers in Ireland to load pages faster. What should it do first?
questions.simpleExplanation: Run the application in a Region near Ireland, such as eu-west-1, so the data travels a shorter distance.

questions.prompt: Which TWO actions improve availability for this company? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy across more than one Availability Zone
Keep every resource in one Availability Zone to save money
Use a second Region as well as the first
Turn off backups to reduce costs

questions.explanation: Multiple Availability Zones and a second Region both protect the application from localized failures. A single zone is a single point of failure, and turning off backups removes recovery options.
questions.simplePrompt: Which two actions make this company's app more available?
questions.simpleExplanation: Use more than one Availability Zone, and use a second Region too. Keeping everything in one place is risky.

questions.statement: AWS secures the physical data center in Ireland, and the company is responsible for securing and encrypting its own data.
questions.explanation: True. Physical security of the facilities is AWS's responsibility, and protecting customer data, including encryption, is the customer's responsibility.
questions.simplePrompt: True or false: AWS protects the Ireland data center, and the company protects its own data.
questions.simpleExplanation: True. AWS guards the building and hardware, and the company guards and encrypts its data.
